output.review_comment:
The input-validation additions (desks < 0, empty headcounts, non-positive headcount) look correct and match the documented `Raises ValueError` behavior. Switching the loop to initialize `allocation` with all teams at 0 is a fine simplification.

However, there's a likely blocking bug: the new code uses `Fraction(...)` but the diff hunk only touches lines inside the function body (starting at original line 18) — there's no accompanying hunk adding `from fractions import Fraction` near the top of the file. Unless `Fraction` was already imported in `allocation.py` for some unrelated reason (unlikely for this small module), this will raise a `NameError` the first time `allocate_desks` is called with `desks > 0`, which would make the test suite fail outright rather than pass — the opposite of what was requested. Please confirm the import is present, and if not, add it.

Separately, since the docstring is supposed to be the source of truth, I can't fully verify from this diff alone whether the new four-level tie-break (`-allocation[team]`, `headcounts[team]`, `-order.index(team)`) exactly matches whatever tie-breaking rule is spelled out in the full docstring (only a fragment of it is visible in the diff). Please double check that against the complete docstring text before merging, and run the actual test suite to confirm both the import and tie-break logic hold up.

Once the import issue is resolved and the test suite is confirmed green locally, this looks close to mergeable.
